chapter: Precision, the union and learning to read
title: Symphonic training does not make a swinger
summary: Crawford says symphony-trained players could not swing, and the blues expose anyone who cannot play them.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Did you all ever in those days, say, in the '30s, when you all got to New York and began to make a name for the band, did you all encounter many symphony musi-

That I don't know, because you never know who's in the audience. You never know who's around. Some fellows had symphonic training, but they couldn't make it in swing bands. I'm talking mainly of whites. They couldn't make it. Swinging is a natural thing. You can't play the blues, you're in trouble. The blues will tell you off, in other words. In other words, show you up. If you can't cut the blues, that includes drummers and everybody else. They don't know how to play the blues, shame on you. Case is closed, yes, sir.
